3. Subsidiary Alliance

EXAM NOTES
  • Introduced/expanded under Lord Wellesley.
  • Hyderabad accepted the system in 1798.
  • Main mechanism: British troops were stationed in the Indian state.
  • The Indian ruler had to bear the cost of the subsidiary force.
  • Foreign relations became restricted and British influence increased.
  • Exam trap: remember the state asked in this paper is Hyderabad.
4

4. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023

EXAM NOTES
  • BSA = Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
  • It replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
  • Electronic/digital records receive legal recognition.
  • The paper's key wording: same legal effect, validity and enforceability as paper documents.
  • Related new criminal-law trio: BNS → substantive criminal law; BNSS → criminal procedure; BSA → evidence.

5. Indus Valley Civilization

EXAM NOTES
  • Seals: Steatite was commonly used.
  • Town planning: planned streets and drainage are major features.
  • Chanhudaro: important craft centre, especially bead-making.
  • Important urban centres include Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
  • Paper trap: the statement claiming massive monumental temples at several major cities is NOT correct.
  • Revision cue: IVC → seals + drainage + planned cities + crafts.

6. Minerals of India

EXAM NOTES
  • Chhotanagpur Plateau is described in the paper as the mineral heartland of India.
  • Major minerals mentioned: coal, iron ore and mica.
  • Kerala's coastal monazite sands are an important source of thorium.
  • Exam chain: Monazite → Thorium → Nuclear-energy relevance.
  • Question type: both statements are correct.
7

7. Demographic Transition Theory

EXAM NOTES
  • Stage 1: high fertility + high mortality → slow population growth.
  • Stage 2: mortality falls rapidly while fertility remains relatively high → rapid population growth.
  • Stage 3: fertility begins to fall; growth slows.
  • Final stage: both fertility and mortality are low → stable or slowly growing population.
  • The transition commonly accompanies movement from rural/agrarian society toward urban/industrial society.
  • Paper answer pattern: 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

EXAM NOTES

  • Khayal is a major form of Hindustani vocal music.
  • Other options in the question: Kirana, Patiala and Mewati.
  • Exam cue: Gwalior → old Khayal gharana.

9. Basketball

  • Each quarter: 10 minutes.
  • Regulation playing time: 40 minutes.

10. Delhi Sultanate — Kharaj

EXAM NOTES
  • Kharaj refers to land revenue on agricultural produce/land.
  • Do not confuse Kharaj with Jizya.
  • Jizya: tax historically levied on non-Muslims under specified regimes.
  • Zakat: religious tax/obligation on Muslims.
  • Khams: one-fifth share of war booty.
  • Exam cue: Kharaj → land revenue.

11. Radioactivity

EXAM NOTES
  • Beta-minus particle = high-speed electron.
  • Alpha particle = helium nucleus.
  • Gamma radiation = electromagnetic radiation.
  • Quick memory: α → He nucleus; β → e⁻; γ → EM radiation.
  • Question asks the identity of the beta particle, not its penetrating power.

13. Government Budget

EXAM NOTES
  • Recovery of loans and advances = Capital Receipt.
  • Reason: recovery reduces the government's financial assets.
  • Interest payments on government borrowing = Revenue Expenditure.
  • Capital receipts commonly include borrowings, recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds.
  • Paper answer: Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Trap: interest payment is expenditure, not a capital receipt.

14. Fourth Five Year Plan

EXAM NOTES
  • Period: 1969–1974.
  • Primary objective: Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
  • Do not confuse with the Second Plan's heavy-industry emphasis.
  • Do not confuse with the Fifth Plan's famous 'Garibi Hatao' emphasis.
  • Exam cue: 4th Plan → Growth + Stability + Self-Reliance.

15. 1991 Economic Crisis — Rupee Devaluation

EXAM NOTES
  • Assertion in the paper: India devalued the rupee in July 1991 as an immediate crisis measure.
  • Reason in the paper is false.
  • Correct economic direction: devaluation generally makes exports cheaper for foreign buyers and imports more expensive domestically.
  • 1991 is the landmark year of India's LPG reforms: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.
  • Paper answer: Assertion true, Reason false.
16

16. Fiscal Policy

EXAM NOTES
  • Contractionary fiscal policy aims to reduce aggregate demand.
  • Typical measure: increase in tax rates.
  • Other contractionary direction: reduce government expenditure.
  • Expansionary fiscal policy works in the opposite direction: lower taxes and/or higher government spending.
  • Memory: Inflationary pressure → Contract; recessionary pressure → Expand.

17. Aditya-L1

EXAM NOTES
  • Mission: ISRO's solar observatory mission.
  • Launch referenced by the paper: September 2023.
  • Objective: study the Sun, including corona, chromosphere and solar wind.
  • L1 = first Sun–Earth Lagrange point; it provides a useful location for continuous solar observation.
  • Paper trap: it is not a Moon, Jupiter or Mercury mission.

18. Electricity — Parallel Resistors

EXAM NOTES
  • Given: R₁ = 5Ω, R₂ = 20Ω, V = 10V.
  • Parallel formula: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
  • 1/R = 1/5 + 1/20 = 4/20 + 1/20 = 5/20 = 1/4.
  • Equivalent resistance R = 4Ω.
  • Total current I = V/R = 10/4 = 2.5 A.
  • Parallel circuit: voltage is the same across each branch; current divides.

19. Plant Tissues

EXAM NOTES
  • Xylem: conducts water and minerals; in the paper it is described as moving from roots to leaves.
  • Phloem: responsible for translocation of food synthesized in leaves.
  • Collenchyma: living tissue providing flexibility and mechanical support to growing parts.
  • Sclerenchyma: generally dead at maturity; thick, lignified walls; provides strength.
  • Paper trap: 'sclerenchyma consists of living cells with thin cellulose walls' is incorrect.

21. Indian Railways

  • Indian Broad Gauge = 1.676 metres.
  • 1.435 metres is standard gauge, not India's Broad Gauge.
  • Konkan Railway connects Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur in Karnataka.
  • Question asks which statements are INCORRECT.

22. Types of Settlements

EXAM NOTES
  • Compact/Nucleated: buildings are tightly clustered, often near water sources or fertile areas.
  • Linear: buildings form a line along a road, river or transport route.
  • Dispersed/Scattered: buildings are spread over a large area with significant distance between homes.
  • Paper clue: hilly tracts + thick forests + extreme climate + houses far apart → Dispersed settlement.
23

23. Temperature Variation in India

EXAM NOTES
  • Peninsular India has a lower annual temperature range than Northern India.
  • Main reason: moderating influence of the sea.
  • Annual range = difference between average temperatures of the hottest and coldest months.
  • Diurnal range = difference between day/night or daily maximum/minimum temperature.
  • Thar Desert has a high diurnal range, not a very low one.
  • Paper answer: Statement 1 only.
24

24. Import Substitution

EXAM NOTES
  • During the first seven Five Year Plans, India adopted import substitution to protect domestic industries.
  • Main objective: reduce dependence on foreign imports and promote self-reliance.
  • Policy tools historically included import controls, tariffs and protection for domestic industries.
  • Later economic reforms from 1991 moved India toward liberalisation and greater external integration.
  • Exam cue: First seven Plans → Import Substitution.
25

25. National Emergency — Article 352

EXAM NOTES
  • Article 352 → National Emergency.
  • Grounds: war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
  • Parliamentary approval: both Houses must approve the proclamation within one month.
  • Approval requires a special majority.
  • Article 356 → President's Rule; Article 360 → Financial Emergency.
  • Memory: 352 = National; 356 = State; 360 = Financial.
